The main takeaway from our work is that
the descending limb of long-loop nephrons is a cation-selective segment, and that this selectivity is not a result of anion impermeability, as has been proposed for other nephron segments.

there are two types of descending limbs in hamster kidney, the short descending limb of Henel's loop (LDB) and the long descending limb of the loop of Henel (LDLU) and the two types of limbs are different in ion transport and permeability.
